newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish lignite miners mull strike against director.
newsitem.headline: Polish lignite miners mull strike against director.

text.p: Workers of Poland's large state-owned lignite mine Belchatow launched a protest action on Monday demanding that their director general be dismissed.
"We have staged a protest rally on Monday. As a last resort, we will consider organising a strike," Zdzislaw Wach, the head of the Lignite Miners' Trade Union, told Reuters.
Belchatow is the sole supplier of lignite to the near-by giant power plant, which produces about 25 percent of electricity in Poland.
The mine's strike in 1994 caused cuts in energy supply to companies and forced the government to import power from neighbouring countries.
Wach said that the only demand of his organisation and four other unions active in Belchatow was to sack the company's director, Jerzy Wagenknecht, over alleged violations of the labour laws.
"We want the director to go because he breaks the labour code, our collective labour agreement and shows no good will for talks with the unions," Wach said without elaborating. @
PAP news agency quoted Wagenknecht as saying that he disagreed with the unions' allegations and that he would not resign.
